summary: Agent 0.34.1 (ADR-0091, amends ADR-0088): a LOCAL SERVICE child's own data folder moves from the agent's data folder to a children's data folder next to it (<data>-children). The agent creates that folder only when starting a child, with a protected access list of its own (SYSTEM and Administrators full, LOCAL SERVICE list this folder only, nothing inherited), and refuses children with data there when it is a link or anyone besides the system and the administrators can change it or a folder above. Each access entry also reports resolve (the real filepath.EvalSymlinks under the child's token; on failure the first folder above the child cannot list) and, for data still in the agent's folder, move_to. Cause: Ollama as LOCAL SERVICE could open its manifests but not resolve them, because LOCAL SERVICE may not list the agent's folder.

findings.evidence: Rollout of agent 0.34.0: Ollama as LOCAL SERVICE reported every manifest as Access is denied; a probe showed open/read/os.Root succeed and only filepath.EvalSymlinks fails, since Go's path normalisation lists every folder above and the agent's folder (configuration, keys) is closed to LOCAL SERVICE. The stopgap was run_as: system for Ollama.
findings.resolution: Children's data goes to a separate folder LOCAL SERVICE may list; the agent's folder stays closed, including file names (listing it was rejected in ADR-0091). Ollama can return to LOCAL SERVICE after its models move.

findings.evidence: Found in this review: users may create folders in ProgramData, so anyone could create the children's data folder first, or a subfolder in it, and later swap that for a link to redirect the agent's modify grant.
findings.resolution: The agent creates the folder with an explicit protected security descriptor in one call (CreateDirectory with SDDL); an existing folder is used only when it is no link and the ADR-0085 exposure check finds nobody besides the system and administrators who can change it or a folder above; otherwise every child with data there is refused without a grant. Inside a clean folder only the system and administrators can create a child's folder, and icacls still runs with /L.

tests.command: go test ./... (Windows, not elevated), go vet (Windows, GOOS=linux), gofmt
tests.evidence: ok; children's data folder derivation (own folder, folder itself and files never granted, move_to for data in the agent's folder), ensureChildRoot (check only creates nothing, created folder protected with LOCAL SERVICE list-only and no inheritance, a folder others can change refuses without grant), existing ADR-0088 tests unchanged.

Skipped locally (not elevated); it runs in the agent's Windows CI job on the elevated runner: a readable folder below an administrators-only folder opens, does not resolve, and resolve names the folder above; once listable it is no longer named.

tests.command: ls-manifest-probe as LocalSystem and as a LOCAL SERVICE process on a Windows node, model folder in the agent's data folder
tests.evidence: LOCAL SERVICE: every open/read/os.Root/DirFS operation ok, filepath.EvalSymlinks Access is denied; LocalSystem: all ok. Reproduces the incident and names the call the resolve fact uses.

limitations: The ADR index check reports a gap at 0090 until PR #142 (ADR-0090) is merged; this branch is updated from main afterwards.
Moving existing data from the agent's folder is an operator step per node (reported as move_to); Ollama's switch back to run_as: localservice is confirmed by the node check during the rollout.
